newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - Firm but little upside seen.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - Firm but little upside seen.

text.p: European physical crude markets should receive some support from scarce supplies for the remainder of the month and demand from other regions, but dwindling refining margins should prevent any further gains, traders said.
North Sea producers and European refiners agreed that premiums for sweet grades were unlikely to rise much further after a storming rally in the last fortnight.
"They're hitting their natural resistance," said a trader.
"There are only a few February barrels left but it will be very tough to better that," said a producer.
He referred to a Forties deal at Dated Brent +54 cents a barrel last week.
The value of Dated Brent was less easy to predict with two big players trying to pull the benchmark grade in opposite directions, traders said.
Two Brents traded on Friday 11 cents apart, at March Brent +44 cents and Mar Brent +33 cents after a deal earlier in the week at +42 cents. Most dealers valued the market somewhere between the two.
But looming bearishly over the market was the fact that four of five Brent dates were five o'clocked on Friday.
In the Mediterranean, pressure on refinery margins because of weak gas oil prices was expected to prevent sour Russian Urals crude from trimming its discount to Dated Brent any further.
"We're losing up to $1 a barrel on Urals and that is the most profitable grade," said a refiner. "All refiners in the Med are seriously considering the possibility of run cuts."

Refiners said they doubted the next Urals trade would be at a firmer level than the Dated Brent less 65 cents cif Med but traders said there was little prospect of the differential weakening with prompt supply thin.
Last week, Syria cut the price of its light crude contracts for February by eight cents a barrel to Dated Brent -27 cents from -35 cents in January.
Libya also cut five cents off the price of its key Es Sider crude, taking it to Dated Brent +5 cents a barrel in February.
On West African markets premiums for Nigerian grades were expected to hold strong, supported by sustained demand from the Far East, traders said.
"There's no reason for the premiums to come off in the first half of March but the Far East will again be important as it was for the whole of February," said a trader.
One equity producer was seen offering early March Forcados around Dated Brent +80 cents a barrel but most traders valued the grade nearer to +75 cents.
Bonny Light was also seen steady around +70 cents.
West African crude exports to Asian-Pacific buyers will soar back above a million barrels a day (bpd) in February for the first time in a year, traders and shippers said last week.
